analysis: Examined the release-provider.yml head text (signing, notarization, staple, final-bytes checks, cluster runtime facts, stage-release and publish-release). The PR changes only three things there: runs-on moves from the Blacksmith Ubuntu runner to ubuntu-24.04 for the resolve/qualify, stage-release and publish-release jobs, and a 90-minute timeout is added to the signing job. The signing keychain lifecycle, the entitlements and get-task-allow checks, the CodeDirectory hash capture and the exact-artifact publication flow are unchanged. The R2 and release-key secrets are still resolved per environment, with PROD/legacy values empty outside prod. Moving the secret-holding jobs to GitHub-hosted runners is not a regression per the supplied evidence, and contents: write remains confined to publish-release. This touches no threat-model assets directly; the relevant context is A-011/A-017 (release registration and build qualification), whose flow is unchanged. The threat-model-review.yml diff is advisory-review CI. It switches the trigger to the one-shot `run-threat-model` label, which only users with triage or write access can apply. It adds issues: write for label deletion, removes the draft check, and removes the 75s coalescing sleep. The label-removal step runs before checkout and uses only github.token with repository and PR-number env values, so there is no injection. The one concern, reported as a finding, is the clearance-mode behavior with a skipped job on unlabeled pushes. Whether the check is required and whether THREAT_REVIEW_REQUIRE_CLEARANCE is true are unverified repo settings. The review scripts were not supplied.

findings.detail: The review job now runs only when the `run-threat-model` label is added (`types: [labeled]`, `if: ... github.event.label.name == 'run-threat-model'`). The old trigger covered opened/synchronize/reopened/edited, and the removed comment explained that in clearance mode an edited PR must not replace a failed required run with a skipped success. The workflow still supports `THREAT_REVIEW_REQUIRE_CLEARANCE=true` (continue-on-error, membership token and the `threat-review-gate.py after` step), so that mode remains in use. If it is enabled and the job is a required check, any push without a fresh label produces no run, or a skipped job that GitHub counts as satisfied. A later push to the head SHA can therefore merge without a new review or clearance evaluation, bypassing the review of provider/attestation-affecting code. Whether the gate is required is repo configuration not supplied here. Fix: in clearance mode, keep the synchronize/reopened triggers, or add an always-running gate job that fails unless a review or override exists for the current head SHA.
findings.title: Label-only trigger can turn the threat-review clearance gate into a skipped (passing) check on new pushes
